🇯🇵 Japan’s demographic crisis deepens: The birth rate has been plummeting for decades, with continued decline in recent years.

Number of live births (approx.):
• 2018: ~919,000
• 2019: ~865,000
• 2020: ~841,000
• 2021: ~811,000
• 2022: ~771,000
• 2023: ~727,000
• 2024: ~686,000 (Japanese nationals)
• 2025: 705,809 (preliminary, including foreign nationals — new record low, 10th straight year of decline)

Total Fertility Rate (children per woman): Fell from ~1.42 in 2018 to a record low of 1.15 in 2024 — far below the 2.1 replacement level (2025 TFR data expected in June).

This is the lowest number of births since records began in 1899, accelerating population aging and straining pensions/healthcare.

Successive governments have tried incentives like child allowances, expanded childcare, and parental leave, but the trend continues. 😔
